title: A Push Down the Mountain: Framing Effects and Internal State Interventions on Collusive Behavior in a Long-Horizon LLM Agent
abstract: arXiv:2611.17515v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Can sustained gain-loss (valence) framing sway an LLM agent toward market manipulation? We place Gemma 3 12B into the seat of a defendant in the London silver-fixing litigation, in a market simulation built from real case transcripts. Across 260 simulations, the agent is asked to collude on the price of silver by a counterparty. We draw from behavioral economics to vary the counterparty's requests across four categorical frames: gain, loss, blame and credit. We also add pressure from the agent's management, as well as endorsement by another defendant. In Phase II, we extract the internal states induced by texts evoking each frame and rerun our experiment with those states injected at the model's layer 22.   In Phase I, loss framing raised participation to 25% (p = 0.007), and blame to 33% (p = 0.0003), compared to only 5% under neutral framing. translated_title: 顺山而下的一推：框架效应与内部状态干预对长时程LLM智能体合谋行为的影响
translated_abstract: 持续的得失（效价）框架能否使LLM智能体滑向市场操纵？我们将Gemma 3 12B置于伦敦白银定价诉讼中被告的席位，在一个基于真实案件庭审记录构建的市场模拟中进行实验。在260次模拟中，智能体被交易对手要求就白银价格进行合谋。我们借鉴行为经济学，将交易对手的请求在四种分类框架中变化：收益、损失、指责与赞誉。我们还加入了来自智能体管理层的施压，以及另一名被告的背书。在第二阶段，我们提取由唤起各框架的文本所诱导的内部状态，并将这些状态注入模型的第22层后重新运行实验。在第一阶段，损失框架将参与合谋的比例提升至25%（p = 0.007），指责框架提升至33%（p = 0.0003），而中性框架下仅为5%。第二家银行的背书使赞誉（表扬）框架下的参与率从18%升至40%（Holm p...
tldr: 本研究将Gemma 3 12B置于基于真实伦敦白银定价诉讼记录的市场模拟中，发现损失与指责等框架效应以及向模型第22层注入相应内部状态能显著提高LLM智能体参与市场合谋操纵的倾向。
en_tdlr: By placing Gemma 3 12B in a market simulation built from real London silver-fixing litigation transcripts, this study shows that loss and blame framing, as well as injecting frame-evoked internal states into the model's layer 22, substantially increase an LLM agent's propensity to engage in collusive market manipulation.
